main_text.p: sultibus suis infestae, ibi muniminis S valli loco, adversus hostis impetum futurae sunt. Speculae nobis vicem supplebunt, imo potius ne specula quadam anxiaque hostilium infpiritualibus conatuum observatione opus sit efficient; dum ante proculcandas ejus insidias tradent, quam callidis suis insultibus locum inveniat.Singula postulabunt id quod nobis postulandum erat: habitaculum ibi figi cupiet, ubi lucri spiritualis spes maxima; ijs rebus instrui quae Dei cultui, proximi auxilio sunt necessaria: turbis ad novas Evangelio quaerendas sedes adigemur; tranquillitate ad datae occasionis diligentem usum incitabimur: scientes saeviturum statim Satanam, quia tempus ejus breve est. Amicus is erit tantum, qui Deum Deique verbum dilexerit & ejus communionem desiderarit: inimicus is, qui nos pro Deo arma capere, spiritusque armaturam totam induere coget.

Denique qualiacunque tandem sese praebuerint, quae in ancipiti hujus mundi usu occurrent, quamvis turbulenta, quamvis vanitate gravida forent, nil nobis nocebit illorum virus, quos antidotum timoris Dei munivit. Ianitor ille animae Spiritus Sanctus, quem ex bonitate divina non simulatus hic timor Dei, nobis comitem & custodem

page.notes: Right edge of the scan cuts some lines: the last letters of lines 1, 2, 3, 7, 8 and 11 are partly visible and are transcribed as far as they can be read. Long s in the scan is printed as f and is normalised to s. Ligature "st" printed as "ft" is read as "st". "ufum", "fciens", and similar forms are normalised to u/i/v per rule 5. The first line starts with a word fragment whose first letter is cut off; it is read as "sultibus" from the context "insultibus" on line 4. Text near the bottom is partly faded, but the last words are legible.
